title: Compute relative Gibbs free energies
action: Using the given transformation enthalpies (Q) and equilibrium temperatures (Teq) for the dimer→fcc, fccl→fcc, and polymer→fcc transitions, and the assumption that the specific heat difference ΔCp is (3/2)R when comparing to the freely rotating fcc phase and zero otherwise, compute the Gibbs free energy differences ΔG of the fccl, dimer, and polymer phases relative to the freely rotating fcc phase as a function of temperature T from 200 K to 500 K. Evaluate the thermodynamic integrals for ΔH and ΔS and write the results to gibbs_free_energies.csv.
description: CSV file with temperature grid and computed relative Gibbs free energies for the three phases.
output_schema: Header: T,G_fccl,G_dimer,G_polymer. Each subsequent row contains temperature in Kelvin (float) and Gibbs free energy differences in kJ/mol (float, at least 2 decimal places).

title: State phase stability ordering
action: Analyze the computed Gibbs free energy curves to determine which phase has the lowest ΔG (i.e., is most stable) as a function of temperature. Write a concise text summary describing the temperature regimes of stability: which phase is stable below ~370 K, which above, and whether the dimer is ever the most stable phase relative to the polymer. Save this summary to stability_summary.txt.
description: Plain text file stating the phase stability ordering derived from the Gibbs free energy curves.
output_schema: One or more sentences of plain text, such as 'Polymer is the most stable phase below 370 K; the freely rotating fcc is the most stable phase above 370 K; the dimer is unstable with respect to the polymer.'
